question.value: How are molecular gas and molecular clouds distributed across the full star-forming disk of M83, and how do they evolve dynamically and relate to star formation?

evidence.quote: This paper presents the first results on the distribution of molecular gas and clouds and their relation to star formation in M83.
Much deeper observations of a substantial spiral galaxy, even a single one, provide an unbiased picture of molecular gas and cloud evolution over a large galactic disk.
The nearby barred spiral galaxy M83 was observed with the 12m, 7m, and Total Power (TP) arrays of ALMA in CO(1-0) under project code 2017.1.00079.S.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2017.1.00079.S.

The three long spiral arm-like features, or bifurcated branches of the spiral arms, in the interarm regions (thick brown lines) are $\sim 1\times 10^8{\rm M_{\odot}}$, $8\times 10^7{\rm M_{\odot}}$, and $3\times 10^7{\rm M_{\odot}}$ for the southern, north-western, and north-eastern features, respectively.

results_numeric.quantity: Fiducial in-situ formation timescale of interarm filamentary structures

evidence.quote: $t_{\rm form} \sim 98\,{\rm Myr}\left( \frac{l_{\rm f}}{100\, {\rm pc}} \right) \left( \frac{\Delta v}{10\, {\rm km \, s^{-1}}} \right)^{-1} \left( \frac{\Sigma_{\rm f}/\Sigma_{\rm i}}{10} \right)$.

findings_qualitative.value: Brightness temperature, velocity dispersion, and integrated intensity (surface density) of molecular gas decrease radially outward from the galactic center to the outer disk, and are higher in spiral arms than in interarm regions.

evidence.quote: The full disk coverage shows that the characteristics of molecular gas change radially from the center to outer disk, with the locally measured brightness temperature, velocity dispersion, and integrated intensity (surface density) decreasing outward.
They are higher in the spiral arms and lower in the interarm regions.

findings_qualitative.value: Molecular spiral arms transition from coherent, narrow ridges in the inner disk to broader, less spatially coherent, flocculent structures in the outer disk, consistent with a transition from density-wave to swing-amplification behavior.

evidence.quote: However, while the arms are still present in the outer disk, they appear less spatially coherent, and even flocculent.

The overall distribution of the molecular structures appears to be consistent with the gradual radial transition from the spiral density-wave picture in the inner disk to the swing amplification picture in the outer disk.

findings_qualitative.value: Massive (~10^7 M_sun), kpc-long filamentary molecular structures are abundant in interarm regions and generally show little or no H-alpha star formation.

evidence.quote: Massive filamentary gas concentrations are abundant even in the interarm regions.
These interarm structures host little or no star formation traced by H$\alpha$.

findings_qualitative.value: Extended, low-brightness CO emission surrounds the bar and spiral arms and likely arises from an ensemble of small, spatially unresolved molecular clouds rather than diffuse gas outside clouds.

evidence.quote: The new map also shows extended CO emission, which likely represents an ensemble of unresolved molecular clouds.
As discussed in Section 9.1, it is unlikely that the majority of this CO emission comes from diffuse molecular gas outside molecular clouds. Instead, it is likely from small, unresolved clouds.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular gas and cloud internal properties (temperature, velocity dispersion, surface density) vary systematically with galactic radius and between spiral arm and interarm environments.
claims.experiment: Jointly deconvolved ALMA 12m+7m+TP CO(1-0) mosaic across the full star-forming disk of M83 at 40 pc resolution and compared radial profiles and regional PDFs of I_CO, T_b, T_peak, and sigma_v across four radial zones.
claims.result: I_CO, T_b, T_peak, and sigma_v all decrease radially from the center (typical sigma_v ~ 23 km/s, max T_peak ~ 16-18 K) to the inner disk (sigma_v ~ 6.0 km/s, max T_peak ~ 8-10 K) and outer disk (sigma_v ~ 4.8 km/s, max T_peak ~ 6-8 K), and interarm structures are cooler (T_peak <= 3 K) than spiral arms.
claims.finding: Molecular gas and cloud internal physical properties change systematically with galactic radius and azimuth across the disk of M83.

evidence.quote: The full disk coverage shows that the characteristics of molecular gas change radially from the center to outer disk, with the locally measured brightness temperature, velocity dispersion, and integrated intensity (surface density) decreasing outward.
Given that the spatial resolution is comparable to the clouds’ typical diameters, these radial and azimuthal variations can be attributed to the variations of clouds’ internal properties.

claims.hypothesis: Massive filamentary molecular structures in the interarm regions formed within stellar spiral arms rather than in-situ, implying long lifetimes (>= 100 Myr) for the structures and their constituent molecular clouds.
claims.experiment: Measured lengths (>= 1 kpc), widths (100-200 pc), and masses (~10^7 M_sun) of interarm filaments and calculated 1D converging-flow assembly timescales in interarm vs. spiral arm velocity fields.
claims.result: In-situ interarm assembly requires coherent convergence over ~1 kpc and ~98 Myr (comparable to the ~106 Myr disk rotation period), whereas assembly in spiral arms (Delta_v >= 30 km/s) takes <= 30 Myr.
claims.finding: Interarm filamentary structures must have assembled in stellar spiral arms and been released or left behind in the interarm regions, requiring molecular structure and cloud lifetimes of >= 100 Myr.

evidence.quote: Building up these structures in the interarm regions would require a very long time ($\gtrsim 100$ Myr). Instead, they must have formed within stellar spiral arms and been released into the interarm regions.
For such structures to survive through the dynamical processes, the lifetimes of these structures and their constituent molecules and molecular clouds must be long ($\gtrsim 100\,{\rm Myr}$).

claims.hypothesis: The radial change in spiral arm morphology reflects a dynamical transition from density-wave behavior in the inner disk to swing amplification in the outer disk.
claims.experiment: Examined the morphological coherence, width, branching, and spur/feather location of molecular spiral arms from the inner disk (r = 80-160'') to the outer disk (r = 160-300'').
claims.result: Inner disk arms are coherent ~600 pc ridges with spurs on their convex sides, while outer disk arms are 700 pc to 1 kpc wide, fragmented, and flocculent.
claims.finding: The molecular gas distribution is consistent with a gradual radial transition from the spiral density-wave picture in the inner disk to the swing amplification picture in the outer disk.

evidence.quote: The observed transition in M83 from the coherent to less-coherent molecular spiral arms from the inner to outer disk may fit to this transition picture.

The overall distribution of the molecular structures appears to be consistent with the gradual radial transition from the spiral density-wave picture in the inner disk to the swing amplification picture in the outer disk.

claims.hypothesis: Extended, low-surface-brightness CO(1-0) emission in and around the bar and spiral arms originates from an ensemble of small, unresolved molecular clouds rather than diffuse molecular gas outside clouds.
claims.experiment: Evaluated CO collisional excitation (photon trapping) and photodissociation/self-shielding requirements alongside the observed brightness temperature (T_peak <= 0.5 K) and beam filling factor at 40 pc resolution.
claims.result: Maintaining CO excitation and self-shielding requires cloud-like volume and column densities; an unresolved 20 pc cloud (M_gas = 1.4e4 M_sun) at T_kin ~ 5 K has filling factor f ~ 1/4 and reproduces T_peak ~ 0.5 K.
claims.finding: The extended CO(1-0) emission is most likely produced by small, unresolved molecular clouds rather than diffuse intercloud gas.

evidence.loc: Collisional Excitation and Chemistry of CO
evidence.quote: Therefore, when CO(1-0) emission is detected, the majority is most likely emitted from molecular clouds, even when individual clouds are spatially unresolved.
While it cannot be proven at our spatial resolution, this cloud-based explanation of the extended CO emission seems reasonable.

why_this_data.value: Fundamental CO(1-0) observations across the whole disk at 40 pc resolution and 10^4 M_sun (3 sigma) sensitivity are required to avoid the warm/dense excitation bias of CO(2-1), resolve typical Milky Way-sized clouds (D ~ 40 pc), and detect the lower-mass (<10^5 M_sun) cloud population.

evidence.quote: A cloud-scale resolution of $40\, {\rm pc}$, the typical diameter of Galactic molecular clouds (cite: Scoville:1987vo), is necessary for mapping the full cloud population and resolving cloud properties
We therefore need CO(1-0) observations to take a full census of molecular gas in galactic disks.

why_this_method.value: Used identical 435-pointing positions for 12m and 7m arrays and full-disk OTF TP scans to enable consistency checks and minimize scan errors; converted TP to visibilities with TP2VIS and jointly deconvolved in MIRIAD because CASA's TCLEAN and SDINTIMAGING do not account for spatially varying PSFs across a large mosaic.

evidence.quote: In this way, each pointing position could be imaged with the 12m and 7m array data separately and together, which is useful for consistency checks.

evidence.loc: MIRIAD Over CASA for Mosaic Imaging
evidence.quote: MIRIAD works better than CASA primarily because CASA’s TCLEAN task, as of version 6.4, does not account for spatial variations of PSF across the mosaic, even though the *uv* coverage varies among the mosaic pointing positions.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: CASA TCLEAN and SDINTIMAGING for mosaic imaging (rejected because they do not account for spatial PSF variations across large mosaics and caused runaway divergences at mosaic edges)

evidence.loc: MIRIAD Over CASA for Mosaic Imaging
evidence.quote: Because of this, we often ran into runaway divergences in TCLEAN, most likely, but not always, at the edges of the mosaic which is covered either by the 12m or 7m array primary beam, but not both.

evidence.loc: MIRIAD Over CASA for Mosaic Imaging
evidence.quote: Even the new task SDINTIMAGING (cite: Rau:2019aa) does not account for the spatially-variant PSF.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: High-order polynomial baseline subtraction on individual TP spectra in the CASA pipeline (rejected in favor of straight-line baseline fits in integrated data cubes to avoid artifacts and improve computational efficiency)

evidence.quote: The data reduction pipeline uses a high-order polynomial fit to individual spectra, which sometimes causes artifacts.
It can be applied to individual spectra as done in the pipeline, or equivalently, to data cubes after their integration, as we did in this study. The latter is computationally much more efficient.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: In-situ formation or stellar-feedback-driven assembly of massive interarm filamentary structures (rejected because in-situ converging flows take ~100 Myr over ~1 kpc scales and feedback models only explain less massive structures)

evidence.quote: Together with the required condition for a coherent converging flow ($\gtrsim 10\, {\rm km \, s^{-1}}$) over a large scale ($\gtrsim 1\, {\rm kpc}$), the required long timescale suggests that the formation of the filamentary structures in interarm regions is unlikely.
However, the feedback-driven models so far explained only less massive structures (cite: Smith:2020aa; Tress:2021aa; Kim:2022ab).

limitations_admitted.value: The adopted constant CO-to-H2 conversion factor X_CO has at least a factor of two uncertainty and may vary with galactic radius (especially in the central region).

evidence.loc: Molecular Gas Mass and Surface Density
evidence.quote: For this paper, we temporarily adopt the consensus value of $X_{\rm CO}=2.0\times 10^{20} \,\rm cm^{-2}\cdot [K\, {\rm km \, s^{-1}}]^{-1}$ (cite: Bolatto:2013ys) for simplicity, with caveats that this value has at least a factor of two uncertainty (cite: Bolatto:2013ys), may vary with galactic radius (cite: Lada:2020aa)

[Note that for simplicity, we assume a constant $X_{\rm CO}$ across the whole disk, while it is suggested that the $X_{\rm CO}$ in the central region could be lower than the adopted value (cite: Sodroski:1995aa; Arimoto:1996aa; Oka:1998vn; Strong:2004aa).]

limitations_admitted.value: Line-of-sight overlap of multiple clouds may affect integrated intensity and velocity dispersion measurements in the central and bar regions.

evidence.loc: Molecular Clouds and Their Spatial Variations
evidence.quote: The integrated intensity $I_{\rm CO}$ map (Figure 5) could portray multiple overlapping clouds along any given line of sight, particularly in the central region.

evidence.loc: Molecular Clouds and Their Spatial Variations
evidence.quote: The $\sigma_{v}$ is measured at a cloud-scale resolution (40 pc) and likely traces the dispersion within individual molecular clouds, except in the central and bar regions where the line-of-sight overlap of multiple clouds may be an issue.

limitations_admitted.value: The cloud-based explanation of extended CO emission cannot be directly proven at the 40 pc spatial resolution.

evidence.quote: While it cannot be proven at our spatial resolution, this cloud-based explanation of the extended CO emission seems reasonable.

limitations_admitted.value: The dynamical evolution scenario is based only on basic timescale estimates and morphologies, using a fiducial convergence velocity surmised from M51 rather than derived from M83's velocity field.

evidence.quote: Here, we simply adopt $\Delta v=10\, {\rm km \, s^{-1}}$ as a fiducial value in the interarm regions, surmised from a measurement in M51, a galaxy with more prominent spiral arms.
The discussions are based only on a basic estimation of their formation timescale and on their morphologies. It is not surprising that some exceptions exist.

limitations_admitted.value: An observatory-announced amplitude calibration error in the 12m and 7m array observations was neglected (estimated impact at most ~0.7% at the galactic center).

evidence.quote: We neglect it because its impact is small, and is, at most, only about 0.7% at the galactic center in the velocity channels where the emission is the strongest.

referee_caveats_inferred: Relative weight scaling factors (5 for 7m, 20 for TP) were chosen by visual inspection of the uv weight density plot rather than an objective optimization criterion.

Beam filling factor f=1 is assumed to convert brightness temperature to kinetic temperature in prominent structures, which only provides a lower limit on T_kin if substructures are clumpy below 40 pc.
Masses of individual filamentary structures in Section 8.6 are reported without specifying the exact spatial/velocity polygon boundaries used to integrate them.
